title: Memorizing music; studio bands sound cold
summary: Memorized music sounds better than read.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Which brings me to the point that all this music that a beginning player listens too, he should memorize. He should memorize everything he can possibly, memorize the etudes you practice, even. Because it is all musical vocabulary. Because I have heard from two extremes, I heard again think of it Toscanini, I heard Ellington say it and come to . /I even heard Benny Goodman say that the best music is memorized music. You know, if you're reading music, it sounds like you're reading it. And good music, a good band -- that's why we were talking earlier about these leaders who come in with studio bands, they get the record date done cheap, they get their taste and wouldn't have to divide it up with their own musicians because they get that thing done in three hours, which maybe with their men it might take a little time. But it never sounded like that band. You could have musicians in the band who weren't half as good as a studio player, but they could play the music every night and it was their music and they sounded ten times -- a thousand times better. You could always tell a studio band,
I don't care how good they played. And even, you know, I took a pride in playing, tried to put feeling in everything I played, but I'd hear it back and I had to admit there was a difference.
It was cold because it was exact, perfect, and everything was perfect (inaudible).
You know, everybody would try -- maybe that's the trouble, everybody was trying too hard.
